rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here بص means insight and also the arguments that produce insight: Qur'anic verses can lift a veil for people willing to see.
rows.anchor: The word ﺑﺼis used in the Qur’ ān to imply insight and also arguments that produce insight

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Prophet is not their keeper comes directly from his tongue; this direct speech suggests such closeness to God that God seems to speak through him.
rows.anchor: It is evident from the words “and I am not your keeper” are directly from the tongue of the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In this way” points back to the preceding arguments for monotheism, prophethood, and the hereafter.
rows.anchor: “and in this way” in “and in this way do We present Our revelations” refers to the earlier arguments

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: درس originally means erasing or rubbing away; repeated reading that dims traced lines gave it the sense of reading thoroughly and memorizing.
rows.anchor: The word درسmeans to erase and rub away.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading can be private or aloud to others, and the Qur'anic terms mentioned here are used in both senses.
rows.anchor: Thus the words R§ and ﺗﻶﻹوةare used in both these meanings by the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic syntax suppresses the conjunctive clause after وَلِيَقُولُوا: the revelations are presented variously so people may understand or admit the Prophet read them thoroughly.
rows.anchor: linguistic principles of Arabic, the copulative clause

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also makes the revelations clear so that people who seek knowledge can learn from them.
rows.anchor: the Almighty is explaining everything so that those who are desirous of knowledge can acquire knowledge from them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger conclusively conveys the truth; “so that they speak out” means their hearts acknowledge that he did all he could, even if they do not say so aloud.
rows.anchor: Here “so that they speak out” actually refers to what they say on their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nation that inwardly recognizes a messenger's complete conveyance yet persists in denial by word and deed is destroyed under God's established practice.
rows.anchor: A nation which, in spite of acknowledging a truth in its heart, adamantly persists in denying the messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must follow revelation and communicate the truth; God could have allowed people their religious choice, so the Prophet should not worry over their faith or bear responsibility for it.
rows.anchor: His sole responsibility is to communicate the truth and this is precisely what he is doing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word و here means guarantor; since the Prophet is neither keeper nor guarantor, he need not worry about them.
rows.anchor: The word وhere means “guarantor.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the guidance in 4:86 and 4:148 after criticism of hypocrites, believers should preserve communication and ceremonial greetings and avoid personal harshness.
rows.anchor: After that, the believers were told that in spite of this criticism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After criticizing polytheism, believers must not let their refutation become so vehement that zealous people abuse the deities of polytheists.
rows.anchor: their refutation of polytheism should not become so vehement that the zealous among them start to abuse their deities.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must stay within bounds even when dealing with an enemy, as 5:8 also instructs.
rows.anchor: it is imperative for the believers to not transgress bounds even while dealing with their enemy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preaching should focus on foundational beliefs: establish that monotheism accords with human nature and polytheism is baseless, and the alleged deities' divinity falls without abuse.
rows.anchor: discussion must be confined to foundational beliefs are discussed so that the addressees are not given a chance to express their violent bias.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abusing deities can psychologically corner polytheists into retaliatory blasphemy, after which they may refuse further preaching.
rows.anchor: they could be psychologically cornered to say bad words about God in their frenzy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though idolaters believe in God, their frenzy and ignorance of God's attributes and rights can make them disregard proper limits.
rows.anchor: when they are not aware of God’s attributes and rights

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abuse is pointless: imaginary deities are shadows, while angels, prophets, and saints are not to be abused; it violates preaching, reason, and justice and can lead to abuse of God.
rows.anchor: If they are conjectural, what is the use of fighting with a shadow?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is against abusing deities, not criticizing them; Qur'anic portrayals of idols' helplessness are a different matter.
rows.anchor: what believers have been stopped from here is abusing their deities and not criticizing them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those they invoke besides God” can refer to hypothetical or actual beings worshipped and invoked by idolaters.
rows.anchor: the verse here refers to hypothetical or real beings which the idolaters would worship and call upon

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because nations cherish traditions and beliefs, humiliating them breeds violence; criticism should be limited to apt matters and delivered politely.
rows.anchor: every nation holds its traditions and beliefs dear. Hence if these are openly humiliated, people become violent.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By attributing the pleasing of each community's deeds to Himself, God points to natural cultural attachment, which helps hold families, nations, and countries together.
rows.anchor: Here the Almighty has ascribed the word “pleasing” ( tazyīn) to His own self.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an recognizes the place of ancestral custom, but requires following only what accords with human nature and God's guidance.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ ān has also accepted the importance of the way of the forefathers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purifying people's beliefs and deeds requires care: remove what has infiltrated human nature against its proper grain without attacking human nature itself.
rows.anchor: it is important to cleanse the beliefs and deeds of people but this task must be done with great care and wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return-and-accounting clause means believers should not overstep in preaching: those knowingly persisting in error answer to God on Judgment Day, not to the believers.
rows.anchor: the believers will not be responsible for them in any way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This accountability is reassurance to believers, paralleling the reassurance to the Prophet in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: an assurance sounded to the believers much like the assurance sounded to the Prophet (sws) in the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding section's logical and natural arguments for monotheism, prophethood, and the hereafter, the next passage addresses demands for miracles despite those arguments.
rows.anchor: In the previous section of verses, logical and natural arguments in favour of monotheism, prophethood and the hereafter are mentioned in detail.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can produce every kind of miracle, but these people would not believe even after seeing them because their hearts and eyes have gone astray, as with cosmic signs.
rows.anchor: their hearts and their eyes have gone wayward

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A settled divine practice brings human and jinn devils to oppose truth's preachers, distinguishing good from bad while giving evil more time to resist.
rows.anchor: devils among human beings and the jinn necessarily embark upon opposing their preaching.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the dispute, the Prophet must follow God's judgment revealed in a Book: the People of the Book recognize its divine origin, while its opponents follow Satan.
rows.anchor: The People of the Book know that this Book is from God.

rows.speaker: Abū Jahal
rows.claim: Abū Jahal reportedly urged God to destroy whoever among them was most guilty of breaking familial ties; he was the Quraysh leader most active in provoking battle.
rows.anchor: Abū Jahal was the most active in instigating the battle. He is reported to have uttered this invocation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Quraysh arrogantly awaited the battle's verdict, the Qur'an says the judgment they sought has arrived; 8:41 calls the battle the Day of Decision.
rows.anchor: the verdict they were waiting for has arrived. In verse 41 ahead, the Qur’ ān has called it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh would stubbornly demand that, if Muhammad's message were true, God should hurl stones or send punishment, after which they would believe.
rows.anchor: if Mu ḥammad’s message has truth in it, let God hurl stones on them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you desist, it is better for you” both counsels and rebukes them to learn from the battle's outcome; otherwise they bring their own doom and cannot harm God.
rows.anchor: The words “and if you desist, it is better for you” are both a council and a rebuke.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We shall also do the same” is an open threat against renewed opposition.
rows.anchor: The subsequent words “We shall also do the same as well” form an open threat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A large opposing group will not help them; greater numbers would only feed God's inferno as firewood.
rows.anchor: If they are more in number, the inferno of God will burn even more, as they will act as its firewood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing declaration that God is with believers is the verse's core: it threatens disbelievers and gives glad tidings that God supports believers.
rows.anchor: The last part “and indeed God is with the believers” is the real soul of this whole verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 20–28 continue the gradual instruction, purification, and reform of believers, openly warning those whose weaknesses prompted the directives.
rows.anchor: The ongoing subject of instructing, purifying and reforming the believers continues with its gradual revelations in the succeeding verses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole Muslim community must stay alert: if some spread mischief and others fail to stop them, the harm will ultimately engulf everyone.
rows.anchor: others did not try to stop them, then ultimately this mischief will embrace everyone
